original_question: Define anisotropic function spaces adapted to ideal hydrodynamics that have higher regularity along flow lines than across them, and prove existence and uniqueness theorems for Euler dynamics in those spaces in any dimension.
target_in_paper: Section 6.4, Problem 16 ("Are Anisotropic Function Spaces the Future of Hydrodynamics?")
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly identifies the target as an open problem about anisotropic function spaces for ideal hydrodynamics, with greater regularity along flow lines, and asks for existence and uniqueness results for Euler dynamics in any dimension.
missing_details: The governing equation should be stated explicitly: the incompressible Euler system ∂_t v + ∇_v v = -∇p, div_μ v = 0.

The ambient geometric setting from Section 1 should be made explicit: a fixed domain or, more generally, an n-dimensional Riemannian manifold M with volume form μ; when ∂M ≠ ∅, the velocity field is tangent to the boundary.
The phrase "ideal hydrodynamics" should be identified with the incompressible, inviscid Euler equation in the paper’s Arnold framework, not with Navier-Stokes or a broader hydrodynamic class.

The motivation for the anisotropy should be made explicit: Section 6.4 ties it to analyticity of particle trajectories, analyticity of flow lines for stationary solutions, and conjectural analyticity of vorticity level lines for GM-flows.

The nearby paper-specific prototype should be acknowledged: Section 6.2 already introduces partially analytic anisotropic spaces X^s_σ, Y^s_σ, Z^s_σ for stationary 2D flows; Problem 16 asks for a genuinely hydrodynamic analogue beyond that special setting.

The refined question should not force hypotheses that the paper itself does not impose: Problem 16 does not specify local versus global existence/uniqueness, a preferred norm, or a restriction to GM-flows.

There are no relevant algebraic parameters here: no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or phrase of the form "for all sufficiently large m" occurs in this problem; the missing information is analytic/PDE and geometric.
refined_question: Let M be a fixed n-dimensional Riemannian manifold or domain (possibly with boundary) equipped with volume form μ, and consider the incompressible Euler equations ∂_t v + ∇_v v = -∇p, div_μ v = 0, with v tangent to ∂M when ∂M ≠ ∅. Define anisotropic function spaces that are more appropriate for ideal hydrodynamics, in the sense that they encode greater smoothness in directions tangent to the flow lines than in transverse directions, and prove existence and uniqueness theorems for Euler solutions in those spaces for every dimension n.
justification: This draft is targeting Section 6.4, Problem 16 almost verbatim. I only sharpened it by unpacking the paper’s background notation from Section 1 so that it becomes stand-alone: the Euler equation, the domain/manifold setting, the divergence-free condition, and the boundary condition. I did not broaden it to Problem 17 on GM-flow regularity, even though GM-flows provide part of the nearby motivation. I also did not add local/global qualifiers to the existence-uniqueness request, because Problem 16 itself leaves that open. The nearby Section 6.2 definitions and Theorem 6.6 show the sort of anisotropic/partially analytic structure the authors have in mind, but they are only a prototype in a special 2D stationary setting, not an equivalent reformulation of Problem 16.
